production.note: Series production started September 18, 2013 in Zuffenhausen; Porsche Newsroom reports the last of 918 cars came off the line on June 19, 2015 after 21 months (https://newsroom.porsche.com/en/products/porsche-918-spyder-manufaktory-end-of-production-11123.html).

body.note: Porsche describes it as a 'two-seat Spyder' with a 'two-piece Targa roof': two removable CFRP roof panels that stow in the front luggage compartment. Classified as Roadster (two-seat open car) rather than Targa or Convertible.

configuration.note: Combustion engine only; two electric motors (front and rear axle) complete the hybrid system.

aspiration.note: Porsche: 'the highest specific power of any naturally aspirated Porsche engine'.

drivetrain.note: V8 and rear electric motor drive the rear axle through the gearbox; a separate electric motor drives the front axle.

transmission.note: DCT is Porsche PDK. The front electric motor has its own single-ratio gear drive.

powerHp.note: Combined system output, published by Porsche as 652 kW (887 hp); V8 alone 608 hp. 887 is numerically the metric-hp (PS) figure for 652 kW and is the figure Porsche used in the US.

weightLb.note: Standard car without the optional Weissach package (3,602 lb with it). Not taken from a manufacturer document - see discrepancies and reviewNotes.

discrepancies.reason: 3,715 lb (3,616 lb with Weissach package) is from Porsche's pre-production specification announcement. 3,691 lb is the production curb weight quoted for the standard car, 3,602 lb with the Weissach package. Porsche AG's IAA 2013 specification lists a DIN unladen weight of 1,634 kg (= 3,602 lb) without naming the configuration; it matches the Weissach-package figure.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 3,691 lb: production figure for the standard car (the Weissach package is an option and not a separate record).

discrepancies.reason: Unit conversion. 652 kW is 887 PS (metric hp) or about 874-875 mechanical bhp. Porsche published 887 hp, including in the US.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 887 hp, the manufacturer's published US figure.

reviewNotes: Curb weight (3,691 lb) comes from Edmunds and duPont Registry, not a Porsche document: no Porsche Cars North America spec sheet could be opened. The only manufacturer weight found (1,634 kg DIN) does not say whether it includes the Weissach package. Confirm against a PCNA MY2015 spec sheet. Also note the US '887 hp' is numerically the PS figure (652 kW), recorded here as the US published rating.
